headline: Permit granted to operate a small residential care facility for up to 16 individuals at 16 Lincoln Street.
summary: The applicant plans to convert an existing family unit, removing one eight-foot wall section, and to improve the building and site before residents move in. The permit runs for 3 years. At 104 Neil Street, a market garden permit also runs three years, and the owner sells native pollinator plants grown by hand to neighbors and landscapers. A neighbor raised concerns about ambulance traffic near Lincoln Street, and the applicant said its similar home on Randall Road had one ambulance call in the years it has operated.
decisions: Approved a 3-year conditional use permit for a residential care facility at 16 Lincoln Street, by roll call vote.
Approved a three-year conditional use permit for a market garden at 104 Neil Street, 5-0.
discussion: Ambulance traffic at Lincoln Street: A neighbor said ambulance calls are regular in the area and asked the board to consider this before deciding. The applicant said its Randall Road home had one ambulance call, and board members said the record suggests staffing would keep ambulance traffic from being excessive.

Market garden traffic and sales: The owner said most plants would be picked up at the curb, with no walk-in retail hours. Board members said the deliveries would not add more vehicle traffic than a typical home garden.
Flowers for special events: The owner said flowers might be set out for occasional special events, but not as a regular farm stand. Board members said that did not seem to be a farm stand.
Neighbor support for Neil Street: A neighbor said the garden brings pollinators to the area and improves the property, and said the neighbors were pleased with it.

Permit type for garden: The question was why the garden needed a market garden permit instead of a home occupation permit. The answer was that plant sales did not fit home occupation rules, and market gardens became a use in December 2024.
